cards.f: Sum of the interior angles of an n-sided polygon
Sum of the exterior angles of any polygon
Exterior and interior angle of a regular n-gon
How do you find n for a regular polygon?
cards.b: n = 360 ÷ exterior angle. If it is not a whole number, no such regular polygon exists.

cards.f: Reason: angles on a straight line / at a point
cards.b: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°. Angles at a point add up to 360°.

cards.f: Which parallel-line reason goes with a Z shape? F shape? C shape?
cards.b: Z: alternate angles are equal. F: corresponding angles are equal. C: co-interior angles add up to 180°.
90°. Reason: angle in a semicircle is 90°.
The tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact (90°).

cards.f: Angle at the centre vs angle at the circumference
cards.b: Angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference (same arc).
Angles in the same segment are equal.
Opposite angles add up to 180°. All four vertices must lie on the circle.
The angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment.
They are equal in length (PA = PB), so triangle PAB is isosceles.

cards.f: Two radii drawn in a circle diagram: what shape?
cards.b: An isosceles triangle, so the base angles are equal.

cards.f: Why do 'Z angles' or 'parallel lines' lose marks?
cards.b: The reason must be the named angle fact, e.g. 'alternate angles are equal'.

short.q: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 150°. Find the number of sides.
Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. Co-interior angles are 3x + 10 and 2x + 20 (degrees). Find x. Give a reason.
short.model: 3x + 10 + 2x + 20 = 180 (co-interior angles add up to 180°), so 5x = 150 and x = 30.
points: Reason: co-interior angles add up to 180°

short.q: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral and angle ABC = 72°. Find angle ADC and give a reason.
short.model: Angle ADC = 180 − 72 = 108° because opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180°.
points: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180°

short.q: PT is a tangent to a circle, centre O, at P. Angle PTO = 28°. Find angle POT, giving reasons.
short.model: Angle OPT = 90° (tangent is perpendicular to radius), so angle POT = 180 − 90 − 28 = 62° (angles in a triangle add up to 180°).
points: Angle OPT = 90°, tangent perpendicular to radius
Angles in a triangle add up to 180°

short.q: Explain why a regular polygon cannot have an exterior angle of 25°.
short.model: The number of sides would be 360 ÷ 25 = 14.4, which is not a whole number.
points: Not a whole number, so impossible
